17283-the-absurd-abc:
Walter Crane's Absurd ABC, first published in 1874, runs the alphabet through nursery nonsense in verse and pictures. A is for the apple, or alphabet pie, which all get a slice of; B is the baby who gave Mr. Bunting long days of rabbit skin hunting; C is the cat that played on the fiddle while cows jumped higher than hey diddle diddle. Humpty, Jack and Jill, Miss Muffet, and Goosey Gander follow in turn.

Crane's pictures and rhymes make the book a classic of Victorian children's printing. Each letter pairs a familiar rhyme with a fresh, absurd twist. Families who love picture books will enjoy a bright, silly alphabet, best read aloud with children pointing at each letter's joke.
18346-null-abc:
H. Beam Piper and John J. McGuire wrote this story for Astounding Science Fiction in February and March 1953. Its opening question asks what happens when learning itself is held responsible for war, one step beyond blaming scientists. The blurb frames the tale as a warning about a world turning against book learning.

The story opens at breakfast with Chester Pelton, his wife Claire, and their son Ray, in a house where a table slides from the pantry and a photocell shuts the door. Ray can tell real bee-comb honey from synthetic food at one bite, and breakfast costs under five credits. Readers get a satire of anti-learning feeling, set in a comfortable future that may soon distrust the very knowledge that built it.
19169-baseball-abc: Baseball ABC, published by McLoughlin Brothers in 1885, is a short alphabet picture book for children. Each letter stands for a baseball word, such as Arthur the running boy, ball, bat, base, and catcher with mask on his face. Only the letters, rhymes, and pictures are present here, so the book is a brief ABC primer on baseball, not a story.
null-abc:
H. Beam Piper and John J. McGuire wrote Null-ABC for Astounding Science Fiction, in its February and March 1953 issues. A note in this copy says research found no proof the copyright was renewed. Van Dongen drew the pictures. A head note frames the tale: reaction these days holds scientists responsible for war.

Take it one step further, the note asks: what if book learning itself is held responsible? The tale opens at a rich breakfast, with Chester Pelton pulling in his paunch. A table slides noiselessly from the pantry, loaded with real eggs, bacon, and toast. Real cow made butter amazes the boy Ray. Ease and anti learning sit side by side.
the-absurd-abc:
Walter Crane made The Absurd ABC for his picture book set, printed by John Lane at The Bodley Head in London and New York, with the book first issued in 1874. Each letter gains a short, silly verse and a picture to match.

A stands for the apple or alphabet pie, from which all get a slice and are urged to taste and try. B is the baby who gave Mr. Bunting many a long day's hunt for rabbit skin. C is the cat that played the fiddle while cows jumped higher than in Hey Diddle Diddle. D is the dame with her pig at the stile. Readers get a daft alphabet for small children, full of nursery rhyme jokes.
